Paragraph: A titration curve graph of pH as a function of the volume of titrant, displays in detail how the pH changes over the course of an acid-base titration. Significantly, the pH changes most rapidly near the equivalence point. The exact shape of a titration curve depends on the relative strengths of acids and bases. Examine the titration curve below:
Question: The pH at equivalence point is
questions.solution: Since curve is given for strong acid and strong base hence, pH at the end point is 7 .

questions.q: Paragraph: Redox reactions play a vital role in chemistry and biology. The values of $\mathrm{E}_{\text {rol }}^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}$ of two half cell reactions decide which way the reaction is expected to proceed. A simple example is Daniel cell in which zinc goes into solution and copper gets deposited. Given below are a set of half-cell reactions (acidic medium) along with their $\mathrm{E}^0$ values. $\begin{array}{ll} \mathrm{I}_2+2 \mathrme^{-} \longrightarrow 2 \mathrmI^{-} ; & \mathrmE^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}=0.54 \mathrm{~V}\\ \mathrm{Cl}_2+2 \mathrme^{-} \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{Cl}^{-}; & \mathrmE^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}=1.36 \mathrm{~V}\\ \mathrm{Mn}^{3+}+\mathrme^{-} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Mn}^{2+}; & \mathrmE^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}=1.50 \mathrm{~V}\\ \mathrm{Fe}^{3+}+\mathrme^{-} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Fe}^{2+}; & \mathrmE^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}=0.77 \mathrm{~V}\\ \mathrm{O}_2+4 \mathrmH^{+}+4 \mathrme^{-} → 2 \mathrm{H}_2 $\mathrm{O}$; \text{ and } \mathrmE^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}=1.23 \mathrm{~V}\end{array}Question: Among the following identify the correct statement:$
options: lodide ion is oxidized by chlorine
questions.solution: Reduction potential of $\mathrm{I}_2$ is less than $\mathrm{Cl}_2$.
questions.source: Most Important Selected Qs for JEE Advanced

questions.q: Paragraph: Redox reactions play a vital role in chemistry and biology. The values of $\mathrm{E}_{\text {rol }}^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}$ of two half cell reactions decide which way the reaction is expected to proceed. A simple example is Daniel cell in which zinc goes into solution and copper gets deposited. Given below are a set of half-cell reactions (acidic medium) along with their $\mathrm{E}^0$ values. $\$begin{array}{ll}\mathrm{I}_2+$2 \mathrme^{-} \longrightarrow 2 \mathrmI^{-} ; \text{ and } \mathrmE^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}=0.54 $\mathrm{~V}$\\ $\mathrm{Cl}_2+$2 \mathrme^{-} \longrightarrow 2 $\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$; \text{ and } \mathrmE^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}=1.36 $\mathrm{~V}$\\ $\mathrm{Mn}^{3+}+\mathrme^{-} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Mn}^{2+}$; \text{ and } \mathrmE^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}=1.50 $\mathrm{~V}$\\ $\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}+\mathrme^{-} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$; \text{ and } \mathrmE^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}=0.77 $\mathrm{~V}$\\ $\mathrm{O}_2+$4 \mathrmH^{+}+4 \mathrme^{-} → 2 $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$; \text{ and } \mathrmE^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}=1.23 $\mathrm{~V}\end{array}$Question: $\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}$is stable but $\mathrm{Mn}^{3 *}$is not stable in acidic solution because:
options: $\mathrm{O}_2$ oxidises both $\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}$ and $\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$ into $\mathrm{Mn}^{3+}$ and $\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}$ respectively.
